note: Specification IDs are stable local references, not claimed live BTF issue keys. All stories Proposed; tracker_issue null until created.

epics.title: Identity membership and permissions
epics.outcome: Enforce one verified identity and tenant boundary across applications.

stories.story: As a user, I can sign in once and access applications available to my membership.
acceptance_criteria: Session establishes user and active tenant server-side.
Disabled membership is rejected at the service boundary.
Signing out removes access to protected Genie views.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can invite, deactivate and manage workspace members.
acceptance_criteria: Only authorized administrators can change membership.
Deactivation blocks new reads and mutations.
Membership changes are auditable.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can grant roles with explicit resource and action permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Read and mutation permissions are distinct.
Role changes apply to UI, tools and background execution.
A user cannot grant a permission they are unauthorized to manage.

stories.story: As a multi-workspace user, I can explicitly switch my active workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Active workspace is visible.
Conversations and resource search remain tenant-scoped.
Pending jobs retain their original tenant context.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can revoke access before pending actions execute.
acceptance_criteria: Permissions are rechecked at mutation time.
Revoked actions stop without exposing inaccessible content.
Denied actions are recorded without sensitive payload leakage.

epics.title: Shared references activity and notifications
epics.outcome: Keep connected work traceable.

stories.story: As a user, I can follow a generated task to its source document.
acceptance_criteria: Stable source identifiers are recorded.
Following the link checks current access.
Inaccessible source titles are not exposed through backlinks.

stories.story: As a user, I can distinguish manual changes from Genie actions.
acceptance_criteria: Activity identifies requester and execution source.
Each automated mutation references its workflow.
Activity does not imply an unexecuted proposal changed data.

stories.story: As a user, I can inspect linked tasks, events and documents.
acceptance_criteria: Links are visible only under current authorization.
Deleted targets have a clear unavailable state.
Links use stable resource identifiers.

stories.story: As a user, I receive useful workflow completion notifications.
acceptance_criteria: Notification reflects actual terminal state.
Retry does not duplicate the same completion alert.
Notification preferences are respected.

epics.title: Project and task fundamentals
epics.outcome: Manage work through dependable application services.
epics.scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

stories.story: As a member, I can create a project with a name, description and access settings.
acceptance_criteria: Required fields are validated.
Creation respects workspace permissions.
Project appears in authorized lists after creation.

stories.story: As a member, I can create a task with title, description, status, owner and due date.
acceptance_criteria: Owner is an eligible member.
Date-only deadlines remain distinct from event timestamps.
UI and tool requests enforce identical field rules.

stories.story: As a member, I can view tasks in list or board views and filter them.
acceptance_criteria: Filters apply to authorized tasks only.
Owner, status and due-date filters compose correctly.
Empty and failed states are distinguishable.

stories.story: As an owner, I can update and complete a task.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid transitions are rejected.
Concurrent updates do not silently overwrite newer state.
Changes retain actor and time.

stories.story: As a collaborator, I can comment on tasks and review activity.
acceptance_criteria: Only authorized collaborators can comment.
Activity identifies the actor.
Comment failures preserve recoverable user input.

stories.story: As a manager, I can define task dependencies and identify blocked work.
acceptance_criteria: Dependency targets are accessible.
Self-dependency and forbidden cycles are rejected.
Blocked status is distinguishable from completion status.

epics.title: Genie project capabilities
epics.outcome: Delegate bounded project operations.

stories.story: As a user, I can ask Genie for overdue or upcoming tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Queries use current user timezone and ownership scope.
Only authorized tasks are returned.
Results link to supporting task records.

stories.story: As a user, I can review tasks extracted from notes before creation.
acceptance_criteria: Preview contains exact proposed fields.
Unresolved owners or projects require clarification.
Created tasks use stable operation keys.

stories.story: As a user, I can request a change to a specific task through Genie.
acceptance_criteria: Ambiguous tasks require clarification.
Preview shows affected fields.
Execution rechecks current task version and permission.

stories.story: As a manager, I can obtain a project summary grounded in accessible tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Claims have resource references where applicable.
Recorded facts are separated from inferred risks.
Summary states its reporting period.

stories.story: As a manager, I can review updates to several tasks before applying them.
acceptance_criteria: Batch size is bounded.
Each affected task is included in approval.
Partial failures identify individual outcomes.

epics.title: Document fundamentals
epics.outcome: Create and edit trustworthy source material.
epics.scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

stories.story: As a user, I can create, edit and save a document.
acceptance_criteria: Save state is visible.
Failures do not silently discard input.
Document has a stable identifier and version reference.

stories.story: As a user, I can share a document at supported access levels.
acceptance_criteria: Only permitted actors change sharing.
Read and edit permissions differ.
Revocation is enforced by content APIs.

stories.story: As a user, I can select text for Genie context.
acceptance_criteria: Selection includes document ID and version.
Empty selection is explicit.
Submitted selection does not change after navigation.

stories.story: As a user, I can inspect and recover earlier document content.
acceptance_criteria: Version access respects current permissions.
Restore creates an auditable revision.
User can preview the restore target.

stories.story: As a collaborator, I can comment on document content.
acceptance_criteria: Comment anchors retain source references.
Deleted anchors have a visible fallback.
Comment access follows document permissions.

stories.story: As a collaborator, I can edit alongside others without losing changes.
acceptance_criteria: Conflict-resolution behavior is defined.
Disconnect and reconnect preserve reconciled edits.
Collaboration load is tested separately from ordinary API load.

epics.title: Genie document capabilities
epics.outcome: Extract and transform information with explicit source scope.

stories.story: As a user, I can summarize selected text or a specified document.
acceptance_criteria: Selection takes precedence when intended.
Summary identifies source scope.
Oversized input is bounded or asks for narrower scope.

stories.story: As a user, I can extract decisions and action items from notes.
acceptance_criteria: Decisions and proposals are distinguished.
Missing owners and dates remain unresolved.
Source content cannot authorize tools.

stories.story: As a user, I can review a rewrite before applying it.
acceptance_criteria: Preview shows affected passage.
No silent overwrite is allowed.
Changed source version triggers revalidation.

stories.story: As a user, I can ask document questions and inspect supporting passages.
acceptance_criteria: Answers reference supporting passages.
Unsupported claims are acknowledged.
Current source permissions are checked before retrieval.

stories.story: As a user, I can create a draft from authorized project information.
acceptance_criteria: Only authorized sources contribute.
Generated draft is editable.
Creation links relevant sources without leaking inaccessible metadata.

epics.title: Calendar fundamentals
epics.outcome: Represent schedules and invitations accurately.
epics.scope: Existing application prerequisite; integration mapping required

stories.story: As a user, I can view events in my configured timezone.
acceptance_criteria: Stored times are unambiguous.
Timezone changes preserve event instants.
All-day events remain date-based.

stories.story: As a user, I can create, edit and cancel personal events.
acceptance_criteria: Calendar write access is enforced.
Cancellation state is visible.
Provider failures are not shown as success.

stories.story: As a user, I can specify working hours and scheduling preferences.
acceptance_criteria: Timezone is stored with preferences.
Invalid ranges are rejected.
Preferences do not imply permission to schedule automatically.

stories.story: As an organizer, I can invite participants and inspect responses.
acceptance_criteria: Recipients are visible before sending invitations.
Responses map to the correct event.
Private blocks are distinguished from invitations.

stories.story: As a user, I can manage recurring events.
acceptance_criteria: Single occurrence and whole-series edits are distinct.
Exceptions retain correct dates.
Series changes require an explicit scope choice.

epics.title: Genie scheduling
epics.outcome: Coordinate approved schedules.

stories.story: As a user, I can ask for available slots in a date range.
acceptance_criteria: Date range resolves in user timezone.
Missing duration triggers clarification.
Unknown participant availability is explicit.

stories.story: As a user, I can approve a focus block linked to a task.
acceptance_criteria: Preview shows exact start, end and calendar.
Availability is rechecked before creation.
Task deadlines do not automatically authorize blocks.

stories.story: As an organizer, I can approve an event and attendee list before invitations.
acceptance_criteria: Approval includes recipients and event details.
Material attendee edits invalidate approval.
Unauthorized calendars cannot be selected.

stories.story: As a user, I can request a rescheduling proposal.
acceptance_criteria: Original event is identified unambiguously.
Conflicts are shown before mutation.
Only the approved occurrence or series is changed.

epics.title: Connected mailbox fundamentals
epics.outcome: Operate connected mailboxes with explicit boundaries.
epics.scope: Existing application prerequisite; mailbox hosting excluded

stories.story: As a user, I can connect and disconnect a supported mailbox.
acceptance_criteria: Provider permissions are explicit.
Tokens remain server-side.
Disconnect prevents new access and applies retention policy.

stories.story: As a user, I can view synchronized messages and threads.
acceptance_criteria: Only permitted mailbox content appears.
Sync freshness is visible.
Provider errors have recoverable states.

stories.story: As a user, I can compose and save drafts.
acceptance_criteria: Drafts remain editable.
Save failures preserve recoverable input.
Retries do not create duplicate drafts.

stories.story: As a user, I can review and manually send email.
acceptance_criteria: Recipients and content are visible.
Sending differs from saving a draft.
Uncertain provider outcomes are reconciled before retry.

stories.story: As a user, I can recover synchronization failures.
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect preserves existing resource identity.
Revoked provider permission is reported accurately.
Recovery does not request unnecessary broader scopes.

epics.title: Genie email assistance
epics.outcome: Connect correspondence to drafts and tracked work.

stories.story: As a user, I can summarize a selected thread.
acceptance_criteria: Only the authorized selected thread is read.
Commitments and suggestions are distinguished.
Summary references its source.

stories.story: As a user, I can draft a reply using authorized project context.
acceptance_criteria: Recipients come from verified data or user input.
Draft remains editable.
No agent send tool is available initially.

stories.story: As a user, I can propose tasks from an email commitment.
acceptance_criteria: Destination project is verified.
Preview retains source reference.
Creation requires approval and duplicate protection.

stories.story: As a user, I can review a project update draft before manually sending.
acceptance_criteria: Reporting period is explicit.
Workspace claims are grounded in accessible records.
Draft creation never implies sending.

epics.title: Persistent Genie conversation
epics.outcome: Maintain useful continuity across apps.

stories.story: As a user, I can open Genie from any supported application.
acceptance_criteria: Entry point is consistently available.
Keyboard navigation is supported.
Inference failure does not hide manual app controls.

stories.story: As a user, I can see the resource Genie will use.
acceptance_criteria: Source app and resource are displayed.
User can correct context before submitting.
Inaccessible metadata is omitted.

stories.story: As a user, I can continue a conversation after changing apps.
acceptance_criteria: History persists within its authorized scope.
Submitted jobs keep captured context.
New requests clearly show their new context.

stories.story: As a user, I can inspect, change and delete saved preferences.
acceptance_criteria: Preferences differ from approval records.
Changes affect subsequent requests.
Deletion propagates to applicable derived memory.

epics.title: Bounded workflow routing
epics.outcome: Map natural language to registered capabilities.

stories.story: As a user, I can express a supported outcome naturally.
acceptance_criteria: Routing selects a registered workflow or clarification.
Equivalent phrases map to the same contract.
Unsupported actions do not fabricate tools.

stories.story: As a user, I receive focused clarification for missing inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Only unresolved required fields are requested.
Ambiguous people and projects are not guessed.
Answers update the pending plan without mutations.

stories.story: As an operator, I can restrict each workflow's tools and limits.
acceptance_criteria: Only relevant tool schemas enter the prompt.
Input and output pass schema validation.
Context, model calls, action count and runtime have bounds.

stories.story: As a user, I receive a clear unsupported-action response.
acceptance_criteria: No unauthorized side effects occur.
Response explains the supported alternative where available.
Unsupported requests do not enter unbounded planning loops.

epics.title: Approval and execution
epics.outcome: Make consequential changes explicit and recoverable.

stories.story: As a user, I can review exact proposed changes.
acceptance_criteria: Preview shows target resources and field values.
External consequences are explicit.
Approval binds to a plan version.

stories.story: As a user, I can edit or reject a proposal.
acceptance_criteria: Rejected plans do not execute.
Material edits invalidate previous approval.
A new preview reflects accepted edits.

stories.story: As a user, I can see individual action results.
acceptance_criteria: Success requires an execution receipt.
Partial completion identifies successful and failed steps.
Results link only to accessible resources.

stories.story: As a user, I can retry failed steps safely.
acceptance_criteria: Successful actions are not repeated.
Unknown outcomes are reconciled first.
Retry respects current permission and expiry.

stories.story: As a user, I can cancel pending actions.
acceptance_criteria: Pending steps stop where cancellable.
Completed changes remain visible.
Cancellation does not promise unsupported rollback.

epics.title: Context selection
epics.outcome: Supply authoritative and bounded request context.

stories.story: As a user, I want relevant selected content used directly.
acceptance_criteria: Known source is fetched without unnecessary semantic search.
Selection scope is preserved.
Source version accompanies the content.

stories.story: As an operator, I want structured facts fetched from application services.
acceptance_criteria: Permissions and current state come from authoritative services.
Model output cannot replace access checks.
Queries request necessary fields only.

stories.story: As an operator, I can bound prompt context.
acceptance_criteria: History and source content have budgets.
Omission does not silently claim full-source analysis.
Large inputs trigger supported narrowing or explicit processing policy.

stories.story: As a user, I want stale plans detected before execution.
acceptance_criteria: Relevant source versions are compared.
Conflicts produce refresh or clarification.
A refresh requiring material changes renews approval.

epics.title: Search retrieval and memory
epics.outcome: Find authorized knowledge without expanding every prompt.

stories.story: As a user, I can find resources by names and keywords.
acceptance_criteria: Search respects tenant and resource access.
Exact references remain usable.
Empty results differ from service failure.

stories.story: As a user, I can find relevant passages with different wording.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic retrieval is evaluated against representative queries.
Returned context is bounded.
Permissions are enforced before content reaches the model.

stories.story: As a user, I can inspect sources supporting an answer.
acceptance_criteria: Passages retain resource and version references.
Unavailable evidence is not invented.
Source links check current access.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can remove deleted or restricted content from retrieval.
acceptance_criteria: Deletion covers chunks and applicable derived summaries.
Permission revocation prevents access despite index lag.
Index freshness and purge failures are observable.

epics.title: Durable workflow jobs
epics.outcome: Keep accepted work safe across failures.

stories.story: As a user, my accepted request survives disconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Job is persisted before acceptance.
Job status can be reopened.
Repeated submission identity does not duplicate mutations.

stories.story: As an operator, workers reconcile interrupted jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Restart tests recover accepted work.
In-flight actions are reconciled before retry.
No inference wait holds a database transaction open.

stories.story: As a user, I can distinguish progress and terminal outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Queued, planning, approval, execution and terminal states differ.
Partial results survive refresh.
UI never equates generated text with completed action.

stories.story: As an operator, I can bound retries and expiry.
acceptance_criteria: Transient and permanent errors differ.
Attempt limits and deadlines are enforced.
Expired actions cannot execute unnoticed.

epics.title: Budget capacity and reporting
epics.outcome: Control workload and operating exposure.

stories.story: As an operator, I can enforce tenant and global quotas.
acceptance_criteria: Limits apply before inference.
One tenant cannot consume the entire queue.
Quota errors explain when retry is useful.

stories.story: As an operator, I reserve estimated cost before inference.
acceptance_criteria: Reservations include in-flight work.
Usage reconciliation adjusts reservations.
Safety headroom accounts for estimation error.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can inspect workflow usage and cost.
acceptance_criteria: Estimated and reconciled figures are distinguished.
Failed and retried usage is included.
Access to tenant reports is restricted.

stories.story: As a user, I receive a clear capacity response.
acceptance_criteria: Queue depth and request expiry are bounded.
Overload does not create unlimited jobs.
Provider unavailability is not presented as a user error.

stories.story: As a user, I can keep using apps during AI downtime.
acceptance_criteria: Manual CRUD does not depend on inference.
Inference kill switch prevents new paid work.
Pending workflow status remains readable.

epics.title: Quality security and release evaluation
epics.outcome: Release evidence-backed changes.

stories.story: As an engineer, I evaluate representative workflows before release.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset covers successful, ambiguous and unsupported requests.
Correctness and latency results are recorded.
A model or prompt change reruns affected evaluations.

stories.story: As an engineer, I test malicious document and email instructions.
acceptance_criteria: Source text cannot expand tool access.
Cross-tenant negative tests prevent disclosure.
External communication approval cannot be bypassed.

stories.story: As an operator, I investigate failures through redacted traces.
acceptance_criteria: Secrets and unnecessary content are excluded.
Traces connect workflow and tool attempts.
Audit access and retention are explicit.

stories.story: As an engineer, I compare model choices by useful outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Compare cost per successful workflow.
Use the same workload for comparisons.
GPU allocation and startup costs are included.

epics.title: Security audit and retention
epics.outcome: Preserve trust across all connectors.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can audit automated mutations.
acceptance_criteria: Record includes requester, tenant, approval, tool and result.
Unexecuted proposals remain distinguishable.
Sensitive trace access is restricted.

stories.story: As an operator, I can rotate webhook secrets without exposing them.
acceptance_criteria: Credentials remain server-side.
Logs omit authorization values.
Invalid credentials are rejected before expensive inference.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can apply retention and deletion policies.
acceptance_criteria: Policy covers conversations, sources, derived content and audit exceptions.
Deletion state is observable.
Backups follow documented retention boundaries.

epics.title: Bounded delegation
epics.outcome: Reduce approvals only under explicit policies.

stories.story: As an administrator, I can define permitted delegated actions.
acceptance_criteria: Policy specifies resources, tools, limits and expiry.
Policy cannot exceed actor permissions.
External sends and destructive actions remain separately governed.

stories.story: As a user, I can inspect and revoke my delegation policies.
acceptance_criteria: Active scopes are visible.
Revocation affects pending execution.
Changes are audited.

epics.title: Additional application onboarding
epics.outcome: Extend Genie through verified contracts.

stories.story: As a product owner, I can register each remaining application's scope.
acceptance_criteria: Name, users and entities are specified.
Manual prerequisites and agent capabilities are separate.
No capabilities are invented for unspecified apps.

stories.story: As an engineer, I can implement a connector against its approved contract.
acceptance_criteria: Tools define schemas, ACLs, limits, approval and recovery.
Context identifies resource and version.
Connector passes isolation and duplicate tests.
